1.title: Widget sync overview
1.excerpt:
Widget sync overview
Widget sync copies widget settings from the Contoso Widget Hub to every device that is enrolled in a site. Each sync run moves through four stages: collect, validate, package and deliver. A run that fails validation stops before anything is delivered, so devices keep their last good settings.
Who can manage sync
Hub administrators can change sync settings for the whole hub. Site operators can change sync settings for their own sites only. Device owners can pause sync on a single device for up to 24 hours.
Settings are inherited. A setting made at the hub applies to every site unless a site operator overrides it, and a site setting applies to every device in that site unless the device owner overrides it. The most specific setting wins.
Sync modes
Push mode delivers settings as soon as a hub administrator publishes them. Pull mode lets each device ask the hub for changes on its own schedule. Mirror mode keeps a full copy of the hub settings on a local relay at the site, and devices read from the relay.
Push mode needs a live connection to the hub. Pull mode and mirror mode keep working when the connection to the hub is lost; mirror mode serves the last copy the relay received.
Use push mode when sites have a reliable connection and changes must arrive at once. Use pull mode when devices can wait for their next check. Use mirror mode for sites whose connection to the hub often drops.
The sync interval
In pull mode, each device checks the hub every 15 minutes by default. You can set the interval from 5 to 240 minutes. A shorter interval delivers changes sooner but sends more requests to the hub.

2.title: Monitor and troubleshoot widget sync
2.excerpt:
Monitor and troubleshoot widget sync
Every sync run writes a status record that you can view on the Sync health page of the hub. A run is marked healthy, delayed or failed.
Retries
When delivery to a device fails, the hub waits and then tries again. The first retry comes after 1 minute, and each later retry waits twice as long as the one before it, up to 60 minutes. After 8 failed retries the device is marked as unreachable, and the hub stops trying until the device checks in again.
The sync agent
The sync agent runs on each device. It has four parts: the scheduler starts each check, the downloader fetches the settings package, the verifier checks the package signature, and the reporter sends the result back to the hub. A package whose signature does not verify is never applied.
Example configuration
The following sync.yaml file sets pull mode with a 30-minute interval and a quiet window at night:
mode: pull
interval_minutes: 30
quiet_window:
  start: "22:00"
  end: "06:00"
retry:
  max_attempts: 8
report_to: hub
During the quiet window, the agent does not start new checks. A check that is already running finishes.
Rolling out a settings change
Contoso recommends a staged rollout for large changes. Start with one pilot site on day 1. Extend the change to one region on day 3, and to every site on day 7. Review the Sync health page before each stage.
